claim: Seed: sector-demeaned vol-scaled 12-1 momentum, 1/vol sizing, 10-day linear decay. Baseline for the keep rule.
outcome: utility 0.402 worst -0.592 (noise band 0.35-0.42 / -0.54 to -0.70). Dispersion high Sharpe -0.42, low +0.87; crash state -1.44 on 112 days. The premium lives in calm, low-dispersion days.

claim: Belief 6 (Barroso-Santa-Clara, Daniel-Moskowitz): momentum losses cluster when market vol is high, so divide the whole book by trailing 3-month equal-weight market vol. Predict: high-dispersion Sharpe less negative, low-dispersion unchanged, worst fold improves more than median.
outcome: utility 0.509 (+0.107) worst -0.446 (+0.146): KEEP. High-dispersion Sharpe -0.42 to -0.23, low 0.87 to 0.81, crash state -1.44 to -1.09. Worst improved more than median, as predicted.

claim: Belief 7 mechanism (Daniel-Moskowitz: the crash is on the short side, past losers are option-like high-beta names): drop the loser leg with max(score, 0) and let the demean wrapper short the rest equally. Predict: crash-state and high-dispersion Sharpe improve, worst fold improves, median falls a little.
outcome: utility 0.229 (-0.280) worst -0.747 (-0.301): RESET. Wrong on every count: crash state -1.09 to -1.59, high-dispersion -0.23 to -0.44, low-dispersion 0.81 to 0.65. The loser leg carries the premium in this basket; the winner leg alone is weak.

claim: Flip of T2: keep only the loser leg with min(score, 0), long the rest equally. Mechanism: if T2 failed because the premium sits in the short leg, this book should hold most of the Sharpe; the crash is still the short side, so predict the crash state stays bad and the median is near T1.
outcome: utility 0.649 (+0.140) worst -0.167 (+0.279): KEEP. Median above T1, not near it, and the crash state went from -1.09 to +1.33 (112 days, noisy). Short losers against an equal-weight long side of everything else beats the two-sided book; the vol-sized winner leg was dead weight.

claim: Belief 2 (Novy-Marx 2012): months 7-12 carry the predictive power, so form on delay(returns(126), 126) instead of 12-1. Predict: Sharpe up, median up; worst fold about the same.
outcome: utility 0.775 (+0.126) worst -0.327 (-0.160): RESET by the worst rule, 0.01 past the 0.15 limit. Median up as predicted, but the intermediate-horizon book has a worse bad fold (2009-2017 fold near zero). Half right.

claim: Belief 2, other half: include the last month, mom = returns(252), no skip. Mechanism: the last month's move reverses (Jegadeesh 1990), so predict lower Sharpe and higher turnover than T3.
outcome: utility 0.444 (-0.205) worst -0.620 (-0.453): RESET. Sharpe 0.42 to 0.26 as predicted; turnover unchanged at 0.04 (the decay keeps it low either way). The skip month is worth about 0.2 of utility.

claim: Belief 5 (Blitz-Huij-Martens 2011): form on the market-residual return, r1 minus rolling 1y beta times equal-weight market return, summed over months 2-12. Predict: high-dispersion Sharpe improves, worst fold improves more than median.
outcome: utility 0.755 (+0.106) worst -0.481 (-0.314): RESET by the worst rule. Prediction wrong: high-dispersion Sharpe 0.09 to -0.03, crash state +1.33 to -0.72. Beta-residualizing the loser leg removes the negative-beta tilt that was protecting the book in down markets; the residual losers crash just like the raw ones.

claim: Belief 9 (George-Hwang 2004): anchor on the 52-week high. Replace the 12-1 return with close / ts_max(high, 252), sector-demeaned, same loser-only sizing. Mechanism: investors anchor on the high and are slow to sell through it, so names far below the high keep falling. Predict: median near T3, worst fold better because the measure is less prone to reversal.
outcome: utility -1.353 worst -3.386: RESET, badly. Shorting names far below their 52-week high loses 4.1%/yr net here, Sharpe -0.83, in every regime. Two causes: the ratio includes the last month (belief 2) and the current-members basket means the names that fell furthest and are still in the index recovered. Do not use price levels as a momentum anchor in this universe.

claim: Belief 7 (Daniel-Moskowitz): hard switch to reversal, where(crash, -book, book), crash = equal-weight market down over 504 days and 21-day vol above 252-day vol. Mechanism: the crash is a loser rally. Predict: hurts, not helps, because T3 is already positive in the crash state (Sharpe +1.33) and the switch flips that; worst fold down, median little changed since the state is 2.5% of days.
outcome: utility 0.618 (-0.031) worst -0.232 (-0.065): RESET, as predicted. Crash state +1.33 to -1.47, everything else within noise. With the loser-only leg and the market-vol scaling, the crash state is already small and profitable; flipping it only loses.

claim: Belief 10: decay_linear is a free lunch while the window is inside the alpha's horizon. Lengthen the decay from 10 to 60 days. Mechanism: momentum has a horizon of months, so averaging the signal over 3 months loses little and cuts turnover. Predict: turnover halves, Sharpe about the same, utility change inside the noise since costs are only 0.2%/yr.
outcome: utility 0.724 (+0.075) worst -0.216 (-0.049): KEEP, just over the 0.07 bar. Turnover 0.04 to 0.02 as predicted, net Sharpe 0.42 to 0.45. The gain is more than the cost saving explains, so the 3-month average also smooths the loser leg.

claim: Belief 11 (size each name by inverse vol): remove the / vol from the sized leg, min(score, 0) with no 1/vol. Mechanism: without it the most volatile losers, which are the crash names, carry the most weight. Predict: high-dispersion and crash-state Sharpe fall, worst fold down, median down; reset.
outcome: utility 0.198 (-0.526) worst -0.852 (-0.636): RESET, as predicted. High-dispersion Sharpe 0.20 to -0.23, second half 0.51 to 0.07. Inverse-vol sizing of the loser leg is the single most important piece of the book.

claim: Belief 4 (momentum in units of own vol): rank on the raw 12-1 return, score = group_demean(mom, 'sector'), keep the 1/vol sizing. Mechanism: without the standardization the volatile names fill the extremes of the loser leg. Predict: median down, worst fold down, high-dispersion Sharpe down; reset.
outcome: utility 0.577 (-0.147) worst -0.227 (-0.011): RESET, as predicted on the median and the regimes (high-dispersion 0.20 to 0.08, crash +0.83 to -1.18); the worst fold held. Vol-standardized formation keeps the volatile names out of the loser leg.

claim: Belief 3 (Moskowitz-Grinblatt, Grundy-Martin): sector neutrality. Replace group_demean with a plain universe demean so the loser leg is the market-relative losers, sector bets included. Mechanism: industry momentum is a factor bet and carries the beta. Predict: raw return up a little, worst fold and high-dispersion Sharpe down; reset.
outcome: utility 0.751 (+0.027) worst -0.758 (-0.542): RESET, as predicted. Median inside the noise, worst fold far worse: a 2000-2006 fold lost 5.1%/yr on the tech-sector short. Sector neutrality is what holds the worst fold, not the median.

claim: Belief 8 (Da-Gurun-Warachka 2014, frog in the pan): gradual moves continue, jumps do not. Multiply the loser leg by the fraction of down days in the formation window, so a loser that fell on many small days is shorted more than one that fell on a few big days. Predict: median up a little, worst fold unchanged; the tilt is mild (fraction ranges 0.4-0.6) so the change may sit inside the noise.
outcome: utility 0.729 (+0.005) worst -0.274 (-0.058): RESET, inside the noise as predicted. The down-day fraction barely re-weights the loser leg; the frog effect, if present, is too small here to pay for 4 nodes.

claim: Belief 6 in the Barroso-Santa-Clara form: scale by the book's own trailing 6-month realized vol instead of market vol. Mechanism: the strategy's vol captures both market vol and the dispersion of the loser leg, which is what spikes before a crash. Predict: worst fold better than T9, median inside the noise.
outcome: utility 0.735 (+0.011) worst -0.558 (-0.342): RESET. Median inside the noise as predicted, worst fold much worse, the opposite of the prediction. The book's own vol lags the market's: it is low going into a crash and high after it, so it scales up at the wrong time. Market vol is the better state variable here.

claim: Belief 11, stronger form: size the loser leg by inverse variance, min(score, 0) / vol / vol. Mechanism: T10 showed inverse-vol sizing is the most important piece, so the book may still be too heavy in the volatile losers. Predict: high-dispersion Sharpe up, worst fold better, median up; turnover unchanged.
outcome: utility 0.787 (+0.063) worst -0.165 (+0.051): RESET, 0.007 short of the bar. Every prediction held in direction: high-dispersion Sharpe 0.20 to 0.40, whole-period Sharpe 0.45 to 0.53, net/yr 1.7% to 2.3%. The direction is real but the rule is the rule; revisit with a cap on the volatile names rather than a steeper power.

claim: Belief 11 on the long side: size the equal-weight long leg by inverse vol too, with an inner demean(min(score, 0) / vol) / vol. Mechanism: the long side is where the book's market vol lives; 1/vol weights make it a low-vol basket. Known: this is a low-vol tilt (Black 1972; Baker-Bradley-Wurgler 2011; Frazzini-Pedersen 2014), widely read and likely priced. Predict: median up through lower book vol, worst fold uncertain and possibly down because a low-vol long side lags in the rebounds where the short losers rally.
outcome: utility 0.636 (-0.088) worst -0.327 (-0.111): RESET. Median down, not up; worst down as feared. The equal-weight long side is the right long side; the low-vol tilt adds nothing here and hurts the rebounds.

claim: Grundy-Martin (2001): hedge the factor exposure of the book, not the signal. Keep the same names and subtract beta times the book's beta exposure, with beta from a rolling 1y regression on the equal-weight market. Mechanism: the loser leg is high beta, so the book is net short the market; T6 showed removing beta from the signal hurts, this tests removing it from the weights. Predict: Sharpe up, rebound folds (2003, 2009) better so worst fold up, 2000-02 and 2008 folds give back some return; high-dispersion Sharpe up.
outcome: utility 0.686 (-0.038) worst -0.290 (-0.074): RESET. Whole-period Sharpe 0.449 to 0.455, every regime within noise; the hedge did nothing and the 11 extra nodes cost 0.033. Either the book is already near beta-neutral (the equal-weight long side carries beta one against the high-beta losers sized down by 1/vol) or rolling betas are too noisy to hedge with.

claim: Cross-sectional z-score of the sector-demeaned score before the loser cut. Mechanism: the spread of 12-1 momentum across names is widest just after a crash (2003, 2009), which is exactly when the loser leg is most dangerous, and the raw score makes the leg biggest then. Predict: worst fold improves, median inside the noise, crash-state return smaller in magnitude.
outcome: utility 0.782 (+0.058) worst -0.210 (+0.006): RESET, short of the bar. Median up, worst flat, high-dispersion Sharpe 0.20 to 0.30. Half the prediction: the z-score helps the median more than the worst fold.

claim: Combine T15 and T18: z-scored score and inverse-variance sizing. Mechanism: T15 re-weights across names (less weight on volatile losers) and T18 re-scales across time (leg size independent of momentum dispersion); the two act on different axes so their gains should add. Predict: utility above 0.80, worst fold at or above T9, high-dispersion Sharpe above 0.4.
outcome: utility 0.806 (+0.082) worst -0.148 (+0.068): KEEP. All three predictions held: high-dispersion Sharpe 0.51, whole-period Sharpe 0.57, net/yr 2.4%. The two near-misses added as claimed.

claim: Belief 2, soft form: mom = 12-1 return plus the 7-12 return, so months 7-12 count twice and months 2-6 once. Mechanism: Novy-Marx finds the power in months 7-12 (T4 raised the median) but dropping months 2-6 outright hurt the worst fold. Predict: median up, worst fold between T4 and T19; the risk is the worst fold falling past the 0.15 limit.
outcome: utility 0.900 (+0.094) worst -0.146 (+0.002): KEEP. Median up as predicted and the worst fold held, unlike T4. Sharpe 0.57 to 0.61. Months 7-12 deserve more weight, but months 2-6 still belong in the window.

claim: Belief 6 with a different state variable: scale by the trailing 3-month mean of cross-sectional return dispersion (the std across names each day, demean(r1) / zscore(r1)) instead of market vol. Mechanism: the loser leg's P&L vol scales with how far apart stocks move, which dispersion measures directly and market vol only by proxy. Predict: high-dispersion Sharpe up, median and worst inside the noise because the two measures are highly correlated.
outcome: utility 1.028 (+0.128) worst -0.008 (+0.138): KEEP, larger than predicted. High-dispersion Sharpe 0.57 to 0.71 as claimed, but the median and worst also moved: Sharpe 0.61 to 0.73, net/yr 2.5% to 2.9%, turnover 0.03 to 0.02. Dispersion, not market vol, is the right size for the loser leg.

claim: Concentration of the loser leg: weight by score times abs(score) instead of score. Mechanism: Jegadeesh-Titman's premium sits in the extreme deciles, so the deepest losers should carry more of the leg. Predict: net return on GMV up, Sharpe about flat because the leg is less diversified, worst fold down a little; utility change inside the noise.
outcome: utility 1.141 (+0.113) worst 0.046 (+0.054): KEEP. Return up as predicted (2.9% to 3.0%) but Sharpe also rose, 0.73 to 0.77, and the worst fold improved rather than slipped. The mild losers carry noise, not signal; the deep losers carry the premium.

claim: Same axis, one step further: cubic weight, min(score, 0) * score * score. Mechanism: if the premium sits in the tail, a steeper weight concentrates further. Predict: diminishing returns; return on GMV up a little, Sharpe flat or down as the leg gets thin, worst fold down; utility inside the noise, so reset.
outcome: utility 1.154 (+0.013) worst -0.080 (-0.126): RESET, as predicted. Return 3.0% to 3.2%, Sharpe 0.77 to 0.74, worst fold down. Squared is the right steepness; cubic thins the leg too far.

claim: Re-test the two-sided book under the current structure: score * abs(score) in place of min(score, 0) * abs(score), so winners are held long with the same squared, inverse-variance weights. Mechanism: belief 1 is two-sided; T2 found the winner leg dead weight on the seed, but the seed had none of the later fixes. Predict: Sharpe down because the winner leg adds vol without return in this basket; worst fold down; reset.
outcome: utility 0.336 (-0.805) worst -1.865 (-1.911): RESET, far worse than predicted. Sharpe 0.77 to 0.01, crash state -2.10. The squared, inverse-variance winner leg concentrates in a few low-vol extreme winners and those reverse; the winner leg is harmful in this universe, not just dead weight. The book stays one-sided.

claim: Belief 2 as a weight instead of a skip: multiply the loser leg by rank(returns(21)), so a loser that fell hardest in the last month (rank near 0) is shorted least and one that has already bounced is shorted in full. Mechanism: Jegadeesh (1990) one-month reversal; the names that just crashed are the ones that rally. Predict: Sharpe up a little, worst fold up, turnover up from 0.02 to about 0.03.
outcome: Session usage limit reached mid-run; not scored. Book restored to T22 for the relaunch.

claim: T25 re-run. Belief 2 as a weight instead of a skip: multiply the loser leg by rank(returns(21)), so a loser that fell hardest in the last month is shorted least and one that has already bounced is shorted in full. Mechanism: Jegadeesh (1990) one-month reversal; the names that just crashed are the ones that rally. Predict: Sharpe up a little, worst fold up, turnover 0.02 to 0.03. 1990s: net Sharpe 0.93 to 1.07.
outcome: utility 1.187 (+0.046) worst 0.269 (+0.223): RESET, median short of the 0.07 bar (a T22 re-run gave 1.182, so the median is inside the noise). Worst fold up a lot and high-dispersion Sharpe 0.71 to 0.90, as predicted; turnover 0.03. The idea is right on the risk axis but does not pay on the median; revisit as a milder tilt.

claim: Belief 3 in the weights (Grundy-Martin): group_demean the sized leg so each sector's longs offset its own shorts; today the long side is the equal-weight market, so a sector full of losers is net short. Predict: worst fold up (2000-02 tech fold), median flat or a little down, high-dispersion Sharpe up. 1990s: net Sharpe 0.93 to 0.85.
outcome: utility 1.039 (-0.102) worst -0.113 (-0.159): RESET, opposite of the prediction on every line. Sharpe 0.77 to 0.66, high-dispersion 0.71 to 0.56, worst down. The implicit sector tilt (net short the sectors with the most losers) pays; sector neutrality belongs in the signal, not the weights.

claim: Belief 10: lengthen the decay from 60 to 120 days. The 1990s rank IC still rises at 20 days and formation is a year, so the horizon is months. Predict: turnover 0.02 to 0.01, Sharpe flat, utility inside the noise.
outcome: utility 1.145 (+0.004) worst 0.145 (+0.099): RESET, inside the noise as predicted. Sharpe 0.77 to 0.81, turnover unchanged at 0.02 (already near the floor). The 60-day decay is already past the point where smoothing pays.

claim: Belief 6, speed of the state variable: dispersion averaged over 21 days instead of 63, so the book shrinks within weeks of a vol spike. Predict: crash-state and high-dispersion Sharpe up, worst up, turnover up a little, median inside the noise.
outcome: utility 1.113 (-0.028) worst 0.156 (+0.110): RESET, inside the noise. High-dispersion Sharpe unchanged at 0.71, crash state 0.92 to 0.96, turnover 0.02 to 0.03. Faster is not better: the 3-month dispersion is already fast enough and the 1-month one adds trading.

claim: Belief 6, strength of the sizing: divide by dispersion squared. One power gives constant risk if the leg's P&L vol is proportional to dispersion; two over-shrink the high-dispersion days where the Sharpe is lower and lean into calm days. Predict: median up a little, return on GMV up, worst uncertain.
outcome: utility 1.123 (-0.018) worst -0.053 (-0.099): RESET, inside the noise on the median, worst down. Sharpe 0.77 unchanged; a 2000-02 fold went to zero because the book nearly vanished there (turnover 0.00). One power of dispersion is the right size; two starves the book in the years the premium is largest.

claim: Belief 4, which vol standardizes formation: a 12-month return over a 60-day vol lets a recent vol spike shrink a loser's score. Use volatility(252) for formation, keep volatility(60) for sizing. Predict: median up a little, turnover down, worst flat.
outcome: utility 1.138 (-0.003) worst 0.101 (+0.055): RESET, inside the noise. Sharpe 0.77 to 0.79, turnover unchanged. The vol window of the formation standardization does not matter at this horizon.

claim: Belief 11, speed of the sizing vol: volatility(20) instead of 60 so a loser whose vol just doubled is cut within weeks. Predict: high-dispersion and crash-state Sharpe up, turnover to 0.03, median inside the noise.
outcome: utility -inf worst -inf: RESET, a numerical failure. A 20-day vol is zero for a name with 20 flat closes, 1/vol/vol is infinite, and the day's demean goes to NaN (breadth 0 on two folds, a +23%/yr fold from one blow-up). Short vol windows need a floor; 60 days is safe in this data.

claim: Belief 3 tested on its own, sector momentum added back on purpose (Moskowitz-Grinblatt 1999): score on the average of raw and sector-demeaned vol-scaled momentum, half sector-neutral. T12 (full sector bets) broke the worst fold, T27 (zero sector bets in the weights) hurt the median. Predict: median up, worst down inside the limit, high-dispersion Sharpe down a little. 1990s: net Sharpe 0.93 to 1.00.
outcome: utility 1.157 (+0.016) worst -0.154 (-0.200): RESET by the worst rule. Sharpe 0.77 to 0.70, high-dispersion 0.71 to 0.53, a 2000-03 fold went to zero. Half the sector bet is already too much; the worst fold is held by full sector neutrality of the signal, and the median gain from sector tilt in T27 is only the one the equal-weight long side gives for free.

claim: Removal test of T18: drop the cross-sectional zscore so the leg's size follows the dispersion of momentum across names again; the dispersion sizing added in T21 may already do the zscore's job. 1990s: net Sharpe 0.93 to 1.18. Predict: median inside the noise or up, worst down a little in the 2003 and 2009 folds, net return up.
outcome: utility 1.010 (-0.131) worst -0.107 (-0.153): RESET. Sharpe 0.77 to 0.66, high-dispersion 0.71 to 0.50; a 2000-02 fold went negative with turnover 0.00 (the leg shrank to nothing when momentum spread was narrow). The zscore and the dispersion sizing are not redundant: one holds the leg's size steady across momentum spread, the other across return spread. The 1990s, with no crash, are a poor guide on sizing-over-time questions.

claim: Belief 10, shape of the decay: ewma with halflife 20 in place of decay_linear 60, same node count. Mechanism: an exponential kernel keeps a long tail of the slow signal and weights the fresh signal more. 1990s: net Sharpe 0.93 to 1.24. Predict: turnover about 0.02, Sharpe up, median up, worst inside the limit.
outcome: utility 1.242 (+0.101) worst 0.122 (+0.076): KEEP. Sharpe 0.77 to 0.83, net/yr 3.0% to 3.2%, turnover 0.02, high-dispersion Sharpe 0.71 to 0.78, both halves up. The exponential kernel is the better smoother at this horizon.

claim: Belief 10, same axis: ewma halflife 10 instead of 20. The 1990s prefer the faster kernel (net Sharpe 1.27 vs 1.24 vs 1.20 at 10, 20, 40). Predict: turnover 0.02 to 0.03, Sharpe flat or up, median inside the noise.
outcome: utility 1.142 (-0.100) worst -0.061 (-0.183): RESET. Sharpe 0.83 to 0.74, high-dispersion 0.78 to 0.62, turnover 0.03. The faster kernel trades more and catches the one-month reversal; halflife 20 stands. Second time the 1990s were wrong on a timing constant.

claim: Belief 2 as a weight (Jegadeesh 1990), re-tried on the T35 base: loser leg times rank(returns(21)). On T22 it gave median +0.046 and worst +0.223. 1990s: 1.24 to 1.43. Predict: median past the bar, worst up, high-dispersion Sharpe up, turnover 0.02 to 0.03.
outcome: utility 1.256 (+0.014) worst 0.326 (+0.204): RESET by the rule, median inside the noise for the second time. Worst up a lot again, high-dispersion Sharpe 0.78 to 0.97, Sharpe 0.83 to 0.86. The tilt is a reliable risk reducer that does not pay on the median fold; the 3 extra nodes cost 0.009.

claim: Belief 2, length of the skip: two months instead of one, formation from twelve months ago to two months ago, same node count. Mechanism: T26 and T37 show the just-crashed names rally, so a longer skip keeps them out without a weight. 1990s: 1.24 to 1.29. Predict: worst up, median inside the noise or up, turnover unchanged.
outcome: utility 1.252 (+0.010) worst 0.058 (-0.064): RESET, inside the noise. Sharpe 0.83 to 0.84, regimes unchanged. The skip does not do what the weight does: the weight uses the last month's rank, the skip only drops it.

claim: Belief 11, the cap instead of a steeper power: winsorize the z-scored score at the 2nd percentile before the squared weight so the leg stops concentrating in a handful of extreme losers. 1990s: 1.24 to 1.43. Predict: Sharpe up, return flat or a little down, worst up, median past the bar.
outcome: utility 1.207 (-0.035) worst 0.193 (+0.071): RESET, inside the noise. Sharpe 0.83 to 0.84, worst up as predicted, median not. The deepest 2% of losers are not a problem in validation; the 1990s over-reward anything that diversifies the leg.

claim: Belief 11, which risk to size by: standardize and size by the sector-residual vol, ts_std(group_demean(r1, 'sector'), 60), instead of total vol; the signal is sector-relative so the risk the leg bears is residual, and a name whose vol is mostly sector beta gets more weight. 1990s: 1.24 to 1.43. Predict: Sharpe up, median up, worst flat, turnover unchanged.
outcome: utility 1.466 (+0.224) worst 0.289 (+0.167): KEEP, the largest gain of the run. Sharpe 0.83 to 1.06, net/yr 3.2% to 4.0%, both dispersion halves above 1.0, turnover 0.02. Crash-state Sharpe fell 0.95 to 0.61 and the first half (0.66) lags the second (1.34): residual-vol sizing lets the high-beta losers back in, which is where the rebound risk lives.

claim: Belief 6, match the state variable to the risk: size the book by the dispersion of sector-residual returns instead of raw returns, since the leg's P&L is residual. Predict: high-dispersion Sharpe up, crash-state Sharpe back up from 0.61, median inside the noise or up.
outcome: utility 1.464 (-0.002) worst 0.271 (-0.018): RESET, identical to T40 on every line (crash state 0.63). Residual and raw dispersion are the same state variable: the cross-sectional spread of returns is mostly idiosyncratic already.

claim: Belief 11, steeper power now that the vol is residual: inverse-cubed residual vol. T15 to T19 showed an extra power paid on total vol; the cap (T39) did nothing. 1990s: return 7.9% to 9.4% at the same Sharpe. Predict: return on GMV up, Sharpe flat or a little down, worst down a little.
outcome: utility 1.410 (-0.056) worst 0.194 (-0.095): RESET, as predicted on direction. Net/yr 4.0% to 4.5% but Sharpe 1.06 to 0.97 and crash state 0.61 to 0.30; the cube concentrates in the lowest-residual-vol losers, which are the high-beta ones. Squared is the right power.

claim: Belief 2 as a weight, third base: the residual-vol sizing of T40 let the high-beta losers back in (crash-state Sharpe 0.95 to 0.61), and those are the names the last-month rank tilt removes after a crash month. On the two earlier bases the tilt lifted the worst fold and high-dispersion Sharpe but not the median. 1990s: 1.43 to 1.57. Predict: crash state back above 0.9, worst up, and a median gain this time because the tilt has more to fix.
outcome: utility 1.580 (+0.114) worst 0.404 (+0.115): KEEP. Sharpe 1.06 to 1.10, net/yr 4.0% to 4.2%, high-dispersion Sharpe 1.01 to 1.24, worst up as on every base. The crash state did not move (0.60), so the median gain is not from the 112 crash days but from the high-dispersion half generally: after any bad month the just-crashed losers bounce, and the residual-vol book holds more of them.

claim: Belief 11, window of the residual vol: 120 days instead of 60, for a steadier 1/vol/vol weight and less turnover. 1990s: 1.43 to 1.47 before the tilt. Predict: turnover down, Sharpe flat or up a little, median inside the noise.
outcome: utility 1.540 (-0.040) worst 0.483 (+0.079): RESET, inside the noise on the median. Sharpe 1.10 to 1.12, worst up, turnover unchanged at 0.02. The longer vol window steadies the worst fold but not the median; 60 days stands.

claim: Beliefs 2 and 3 together: the last-month tilt measured relative to the sector, rank(group_demean(returns(21), 'sector')), because the one-month reversal is stock-specific while the sector part of the move continues (Moskowitz-Grinblatt). 1990s: 1.57 to 1.71. Predict: Sharpe up, median up, high-dispersion up.
outcome: utility 1.554 (-0.026) worst 0.214 (-0.190): RESET by both rules. Sharpe unchanged at 1.11, high-dispersion 1.24 to 1.17, a 2000-02 fold went to turnover 0.00. Removing the sector part of the last month's move loses the part of the tilt that protects the worst fold: in a sector-wide crash month every name in the sector bounces, and the raw rank keeps all of them out of the leg. Third time the 1990s mis-ranked a tilt variant.

claim: Belief 9 on the low: multiply the leg by one minus the fraction of the year since the 52-week low, so a loser at a fresh low is shorted in full and one that bottomed months ago and is recovering is shorted less (George-Hwang anchoring, on the low). 1990s: 1.57 to 1.72. Predict: median up, worst flat or up.
outcome: utility 1.429 (-0.151) worst 0.238 (-0.166): RESET by both rules. Sharpe 1.10 to 1.04, a 2000-06 fold went negative, 7 extra nodes cost 0.021. Names at a fresh 52-week low are the ones that bounce in this universe, as T7 found for the high; price-level anchors do not work on a current-members basket. Fourth tilt the 1990s mis-ranked.

claim: Beliefs 3 and 4, standardize within the sector: z-score the vol-scaled momentum inside each sector (sector demean over sector root-mean-square via group_sum and is_valid) instead of a universe z-score after the sector demean, so every sector gets the same share of the loser leg. Predict: worst up, sector concentration down, median inside the noise or up. (Two earlier commits, 1c6653f and 6e1b6ba, did not parse: group_std and group_count_valid are rolling operators.)
outcome: utility 1.330 (-0.250) worst 0.247 (-0.157): RESET by both rules. Sharpe 1.10 to 0.88, low-dispersion Sharpe 0.98 to 0.79, 9 extra nodes. Equalizing sectors removes the implicit tilt toward the sector with the widest momentum spread, which T27 showed pays. The universe z-score after the sector demean stands.

claim: Removal test of T22 on the residual-vol base: drop the squared weight, linear loser score times the tilt. T22's mechanism says the deep losers carry the premium so the median falls; the 1990s say the opposite (1.57 to 1.71). Predict: median inside the noise or down.
outcome: utility 1.267 (-0.313) worst 0.251 (-0.153): RESET. Sharpe 1.10 to 0.92, low-dispersion Sharpe 0.98 to 0.73. The squared weight is not redundant with residual-vol sizing: the premium sits in the deep losers on every base, and the 1990s were wrong a fifth time.

claim: Belief 6 in the Cooper-Gutierrez-Hameed (2004) form: halve the book when the equal-weight market is down over the past year, since momentum profits in their data follow up markets only. Predict: reset; the loser leg earns most in the bear folds (2001-02, 2008), so the median falls and the 2000-02 fold weakens.
outcome: utility 1.519 (-0.061) worst 0.286 (-0.118): RESET, as predicted. Sharpe 1.10 unchanged, turnover 0.02 to 0.03, crash state 0.60 unchanged, a 2003-07 fold fell to 0.2; 7 extra nodes cost 0.021. The down-market state is where the loser-only leg is safest, the opposite of a two-sided momentum book.

claim: Belief 2 removal test on the current base: drop the extra months 7-12 term, plain 12-1 formation. T20 found the double weight worth +0.094 on an older base. Predict: median down by about that, worst flat.
outcome: utility 1.444 (-0.136) worst 0.256 (-0.148): RESET, as predicted. Sharpe 1.10 to 1.05, crash state 0.60 to 0.45. The months 7-12 weight is worth more now than when it was added; Novy-Marx's horizon holds on every base.

claim: Robustness of the cross-sectional scale: divide the sector-demeaned momentum by its mean absolute deviation instead of its std, since the std is inflated by the winner tail (1999-2000, 2009) and shrinks the loser leg exactly then. 1990s: 1.57 to 1.71. Predict: median up, worst flat.
outcome: utility 1.569 (-0.011) worst 0.412 (+0.008): RESET, inside the noise. Sharpe 1.10 to 1.13 but 3 extra nodes cost 0.009 and the median did not move. The winner tail does not distort the zscore enough to matter.

claim: Belief 11 flipped into a signal (Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang 2006): tilt the leg toward names whose residual vol is rising against its own year, rank of 60-day over 252-day residual vol; rising idiosyncratic vol in a loser is distress. 1990s: 1.57 to 1.66. Predict: median up a little, worst and crash state down.
outcome: utility 1.266 (-0.314) worst 0.326 (-0.078): RESET. Sharpe 1.10 to 0.99, a 2000-02 fold with turnover 0.00 (the leg shrank to nothing when every loser's vol was rising together). Vol trend is a market-wide state here, not a stock-level one, and the tilt doubles as a bad sizing rule. Sixth tilt the 1990s mis-ranked.

claim: Belief 6 removal test: drop the dispersion sizing so the book has constant gross. T21 found it worth +0.128 on the T20 base, mostly in the worst fold and the high-dispersion half. Predict: worst falls below the limit, high-dispersion Sharpe down, median down.
outcome: utility 1.607 (+0.027) worst 0.470 (+0.066): RESET by the rule (median inside the noise), but the prediction was wrong on every line: Sharpe 1.10 to 1.15, high-dispersion 1.24 to 1.28, worst up, 5 nodes fewer. On the residual-vol base with the last-month tilt the dispersion sizing is redundant: the tilt already shrinks the leg after a bad month, and residual vol already discounts the names that spike. The simpler book is as good; the rule keeps T43 because the gain is inside the noise.

claim: Belief 6, hard form (Daniel-Moskowitz state): halve the book when the market is down over two years and one-month vol is above one-year vol; 112 of 4528 days, Sharpe 0.60 there against 1.11 elsewhere. Predict: crash contribution halves, median inside the noise (2.5% of days), worst flat; 14 extra nodes cost 0.04.
outcome: utility 1.553 (-0.027) worst 0.311 (-0.093): RESET, inside the noise as predicted. Crash-state net/yr 1.0% to 0.5%, everything else unchanged, charge 0.078 to 0.108. The state is too rare to pay for its own nodes; the continuous sizing already covers it.

claim: Belief 10, one step the other way from T36: ewma halflife 30 instead of 20. Predict: turnover 0.02 to 0.01, median inside the noise.
outcome: utility 1.575 (-0.005) worst 0.514 (+0.110): RESET, inside the noise as predicted. Sharpe 1.10 to 1.13, turnover unchanged at 0.02, worst up. Halflife 20 to 30 is flat; the kernel is on a plateau.

claim: Belief 2, one more step on the Novy-Marx weight: months 7-12 counted three times against months 2-6 once. T20 found 2x worth +0.094 and T50 found the term worth 0.13 on this base. Predict: diminishing returns, median inside the noise or slightly up, worst flat.
outcome: utility 1.616 (+0.036) worst 0.327 (-0.077): RESET, inside the noise as predicted. Sharpe 1.10 unchanged, regimes unchanged. Two-to-one is as far as the weight goes.

claim: Belief 4 applied to the tilt: rank the last month's move in units of the stock's own residual vol, rank(returns(21) / vol), so a 10% drop is a crash for a utility and a shrug for a biotech. Predict: median inside the noise or up a little, worst flat.
outcome: utility 1.644 (+0.064) worst 0.504 (+0.100): RESET by the rule, 0.006 short of the bar (as T15 was). Every line improved: Sharpe 1.10 to 1.17, net/yr 4.2% to 4.6%, crash state 0.60 to 0.91, high-dispersion 1.24 to 1.35. The vol-scaled last month is the better measure of "just crashed"; a near-miss to combine.

claim: Combine T57 and T53: the vol-scaled last-month tilt and no dispersion sizing. One re-weights names within the leg, the other removes a book-level scaling that T53 showed is redundant on this base. T57 was 0.006 short with 2 extra nodes, T53 +0.027 with 5 fewer. Predict: utility above the bar, worst at or above T43, crash state near 0.9.
outcome: utility 1.740 (+0.160) worst 0.477 (+0.073): KEEP, as T19 did for its pair of near-misses. Sharpe 1.10 to 1.22, net/yr 4.2% to 4.8%, crash state 0.91, high-dispersion 1.40, 22 nodes. The book no longer sizes itself by any market state: residual-vol sizing plus the vol-scaled last-month tilt handle the crash on their own.

claim: Belief 2's mechanism on the long side (Jegadeesh 1990): add a small long leg of last month's vol-scaled dippers across all names, one tenth the scale of the loser leg. Known to have decayed after 2000 (Nagel 2012). Predict: median inside the noise or slightly up, turnover up a little, worst flat.
outcome: utility 1.739 (-0.001) worst 0.562 (+0.085): RESET, inside the noise as predicted. Sharpe 1.22 to 1.24, turnover 0.02 to 0.03, 5 extra nodes cost 0.015, worst up. The long-side reversal is real but small and no longer pays for its nodes in this period.

claim: Removal test of T18's zscore on the final base: T34 found it worth 0.13 with the dispersion sizing present; now nothing else holds the leg's size steady across the spread of momentum. Predict: a larger fall in the median and the worst fold, two fewer nodes.
outcome: utility 1.550 (-0.190) worst 0.387 (-0.090): RESET, as predicted and larger than T34. Sharpe 1.22 to 1.10, crash state 0.91 to 0.48. The cross-sectional zscore is the one piece of time-variation the book needs. Final book is T58.
